PKG01.finding: Version-only admission does not bind the executable to current dirty source/resource inputs; absent ProductVersion is not rejected. CI's build-before-package ordering is useful but no successful-build receipt exists. A signature proves artifact integrity, not that intended source was built.
PKG01.hardlinkCompatibility: Read-only fsutil inspection found the existing Cargo release executable linked at target/release/atsumi.exe and target/release/deps/atsumi.exe. The newly strict package handle boundary correctly refuses this two-link input, so an explicit build-output capture step is required before real packaging. Do not silently weaken the resource boundary, break links or delete Cargo output.
minimumPlan: Add one explicit successful-build wrapper/receipt schema. Before invoking the approved build, snapshot a positive input manifest; after success recheck that manifest unchanged and record output hashes, target, compiler/SDK versions, flags/config and dependency lock/resource manifests. Missing or failed build produces no success receipt.

Include app/frontend/native sources, public assets, vendor patches/licenses, icons/capabilities, build/config/lock files and the exact approved tool manifests. Record source content digests including dirty files, not only git HEAD or mtime. Include newly added/missing input detection. Never capture the whole environment, user .runtime tree, profile, cookies, DB, media or signing secrets.

Under a held read-only handle and explicit successful-build ownership, capture the known Cargo output bytes into a new single-link .runtime/release-inputs/<buildUUID>/atsumi.exe. Bind capture hash to the successful output and receipt. This narrowly admits the build tool's known two-link output only for capture; generic resource proof/copy still rejects hardlinks.

Make portable/installer release admission require the receipt and captured output, recheck source/resource/output bytes immediately before packaging and signing, and retain the receipt as release provenance. Use new stages and fail without replacing existing packages. Actual build and acceptance need separate authority.
